question: What was the term of the Central Legislative Assembly under the Government of India Act of 1919?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act of 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, established a bicameral legislature in India.
 
• Under this act, the Central Legislative Assembly was created as the lower house of the Indian legislature.
 
• The term of the Central Legislative Assembly was set to three years.
 
• The act aimed to introduce a measure of self-governance in India and increase Indian participation in governance.
 
• The Assembly had 145 members, with 104 elected and 41 nominated by the Governor-General.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms:**

 
 
• These reforms were named after Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy of India.
 
• The reforms were aimed at giving more representation to Indians in governance and were a response to the growing demand for self-rule.
 
• The reforms led to the establishment of a dual government system, known as diarchy, in the provinces.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1919:**
 
 
• This act was a significant step towards constitutional reforms in India.
 
• It introduced a bicameral legislature at the center consisting of the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Act also expanded the participation of Indians in the governance process through increased legislative membership and electoral provisions.
 
 
 
• **Diarchy:**
 
 
• Under the Government of India Act 1919, diarchy was introduced in the provincial governments.
 
• It meant a division of subjects into "transferred" and "reserved" categories.
 
• Transferred subjects were administered by Indian ministers, whereas reserved subjects remained under the control of the British Governors.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Act:**
 
 
• The Act was seen as inadequate by many Indian leaders as it did not grant full self-governance.
 
• It led to increased political activities and the rise of movements demanding complete independence.
 
• The Act paved the way for future reforms, including the Government of India Act 1935.
